summary:
To address the challenges of harsh space environments, costly Earth resupplies, and abstract space education for youth, this project presents a 2D Pixel Art survival simulation game. Players take the role of a stranded space explorer on an uncharted planet after a spacecraft crash. To survive and return to Earth, they must gather local minerals, craft components, build automated bases, research planetary conditions using rovers and drones, and defend against environmental hazards and rival groups.
Scientifically grounded in In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), the game integrates NASA concepts: translating the Science Missions R&D process into gameplay, modeling BioNutrients for microbial food production, and applying Mission Design Lab trade-offs to optimize scarce resources. Ultimately, the project promotes STEM education, problem-solving, and understanding of off-Earth sustainability, with future plans to add real NASA terrain data, multiple planets, tech upgrades, and multiplayer mode.

Project NameSTART - A - LITE
  1. High-Level Summary

This project develops START - A - LITE, a 2D survival game featuring Pixel Art graphics where players roleplay as a space explorer stranded on an unfamiliar planet following a spacecraft malfunction. Players navigate planetary challenges by building base infrastructure, managing resources, conducting environmental research, and repairing their spacecraft to safely return to Earth. The game integrates In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) concepts to educate players on space science, technology, resource management, and survival in extreme environments.

  • Final Project: [Final Project Source Code / Game Link]
  1. Project Details

1. Problem & Objectives: Long-duration space exploration presents challenges such as extreme environmental survival (acid rain, dust storms, radiation, volcanic activity), resource scarcity, complex base construction, technical risks, and abstract public understanding of space missions. The game addresses these issues by translating space mission workflows and survival mechanisms into interactive gameplay.

2. Key Game Mechanisms: Players must fulfill three primary objectives: survival (managing oxygen, food, water, and power), exploration & research (gathering terrain, climate, and mineral data using rovers, drones, and sensors), and spacecraft restoration. Core mechanics include resource extraction (iron, copper, water, sulfur, petroleum, nitrogen), base automation, factory manufacturing, and defense against competing factions.

3. Innovation & Impact: Features In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) to demonstrate space autonomy. Serves as an interactive STEM educational tool promoting problem-solving, science literacy, and resource management.

  1. Use of AI

AI technologies and generative tools can be utilized during game development for generating Pixel Art assets, optimizing pathfinding algorithms for automated rovers and drones, and procedural generation of terrain and environmental events.

NASA & Partner Data Integration

  • BioNutrients Concept: Inspired by NASA BioNutrients research for producing nutrients in space via microbial growth in bioreactors (Raw materials -> BioReactor -> BioNutrients).
  • NASA Mission Design Lab Methodology: Implements Trade-off Systems (balancing resource location vs. automation effort) and strict Resource Management strategies.
  • Future NASA Data Integration: Future developments aim to incorporate NASA planetary terrain data, satellite imagery, and scientific mission parameters directly into map generation.

References

  1. NASA BioNutrients Project & In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) Research.
  2. NASA Mission Design Lab (Trade-off Systems & Resource Management Frameworks).
